title: Big touring bands of the 1930s: McKinney's, Henderson, Ellington
summary: He recalls the big road bands of the 30s, naming McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Fletcher Henderson, Duke Ellington, Alphonso Trent and Noble Sissle, and Goldkette's booking.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Um, when you were traveling on the, traveling around Mainland 30s, were there a lot of traveling
You said there were two boats and four bands. But you know.

Well the two biggest bands that I remember, or not the two bands, I had a whole lot of bands that traveled but they were big bands you see. But we had regular work. But these other jobs they had one-nighters like Fletcher Henderson, McKinney's Cotton Pickers. They were the first bands that I can remember during the time, that they got a thousand dollars a night. That was a whole lot of money for a band. Way back there. Well I think they had a band they called Gene Goldkatt out of Detroit, that's where this band McKinney is. And I think they were booking them out there. So Gene Goldkatt had a whole lot of bands under their name, like the Preservation Hall. See they had two or three bands and that's what they did. Gene Goldkatt had bands different places. Yeah they had a whole lot of bands. They had a whole lot of bands come out of Florida. They had a hell of a band. They had a whole lot of bands on the radio. Al Ponce O' Trent come out of Texas, and a hell of a band. Second to none of the bands. That's second to Duke Allington and none of the rest of them. Duke Allington was on the road. That's another, Duke Allington was tops at the time you see. But they had other bands. I had occasion to listen to the three top bands at that time. That was McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Duke Allington, and Fletcher Henderson on the one road. It was great. Then you had Noble Sisterly had a band on the road. They had a whole lot of bands on the road. Larry James had a big band, as many of them. Glenn Miller, they had a whole lot of bands out on the road. Some of them did one-nighters and some of them did out of the Goldwick.
